Anya Patel: Heads-up — bringing up r2b-int8 (per-channel 4-bit quant) on the multilingual embed onboarding suite. Quick local eval shows recall@10 drop vs r2b-fp16 baseline across en/es/jp holdout. posting quick numbers and logs below. Anyone seen similar pattern with per-channel quant? :thinking_face:

Mike Chen: Did you confirm identical preprocessing + normalization? and which quant backend was used (pt-quant / onnx)?

Anya Patel: same preprocessing pipeline, embed-harness v0.9.3, tokenizer normalized. backend: pt-q + custom kernel. baseline run_id: baseline-20260312-a1, this run: r2b-int8-1987659999

Anya Patel: eval command I ran:
```
python -m eval_harness.run \
  --model r2b-int8:latest \
  --holdout multilingual_holdout_2026.json \
  --metrics recall@10,recall@1,cosine_mean,cosine_std \
  --out s3://redwood-evals/r2b-int8/1987659999/summary.json
```

Anya Patel: raw summary (excerpt):
```
baseline fp16: recall@10 = 0.912, recall@1 = 0.678, cosine_mean = 0.412
r2b-int8 : recall@10 = 0.877, recall@1 = 0.655, cosine_mean = 0.398
per-language diffs (recall@10): en -0.018, es -0.050, jp -0.040
```

Devendra Rao: That magnitude on es/jp suggests quant noise correlated with low-resource lang subspace. Can you dump per-layer scale & zero-point stats? I want to check LayerNorm/gamma scaling and any outlier activations.

Anya Patel: grabbing stats now. small snippet from layer-stats (top-K outliers):
```
layer.5.attn_out scale_mean=0.012 scale_std=0.008 outlier_count=3
layer.9.mlp_fc2 scale_mean=0.045 scale_std=0.12 outlier_count=12 <-- suspicious
```

eval-bot: New artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/r2b-int8/1987659999/layer_stats.json :white_check_mark:

Lina Gomez: Also run clustering/kmeans purity on the holdout. Quantization often shifts centroids for long-tail languages. Purity drop can explain recall falls.

Anya Patel: quick kmeans purity (k=100, 50k samples):
```
purity baseline fp16: en 0.86, es 0.83, jp 0.79
purity r2b-int8: en 0.85, es 0.78, jp 0.72
```

Mike Chen: Okay, asymmetric vs symmetric quant might help — asymmetric often preserves small-magnitude gradients for jp/es tokens. Also try per-channel vs per-tensor toggles. Can you run an asymmetric-perchannel sweep?

Devendra Rao: Also compare ONNX runtime with our native kernel. We saw kernel ordering mismatch cause ~2-3% recall delta in last quarter for a different model. Run onnx export + run the eval harness with ORT backend.

Anya Patel: scheduling overnight jobs: asymmetric-perchannel sweep + onnx-ort compare. leaving commands here:
```
# asymmetric sweep
python -m quant_tools.sweep \
  --model r2b-fp16:checkpoint \
  --modes asymmetric_per_channel,symmetric_per_channel \
  --calib-dataset multilingual_calib_10k.json \
  --out-dir /tmp/quant_sweeps/1987659999

# onnx export + eval
python -m model_export.export_onnx --model r2b-int8 --out r2b-int8.onnx --quant backend=ptq
python -m eval_harness.run --model r2b-int8.onnx --backend ort --holdout multilingual_holdout_2026.json --out s3://redwood-evals/r2b-int8/1987659999/onnx_summary.json
```

eval-bot: Job scheduled: eval-harness job_id=98765 (asymmetric sweep). ETA ~8h.

Mike Chen: Great. If asymmetric-per-channel doesn't help, try small fp16 hybrid for top-2 layers — those often control cross-lingual alignment.

Anya Patel: noted. I'll do fp16-hybrid fallback after sweep if needed. Plan: 1) asymmetric-per-channel sweep 2) ORT vs native compare 3) fp16-hybrid for top2. Will post results tomorrow morning (UTC).

Devendra Rao: one more: capture nearest-neighbor distance histograms per-language (baseline vs int8) — a simple shift in mean distance explains recall drop.

Anya Patel: already logging that, attaching histogram link once job finishes.

eval-bot: Job finished: eval-harness job_id=98765, results: s3://redwood-evals/r2b-int8/1987659999/summary_sweep.json

Anya Patel: quick post-sweep notes: asymmetric-per-channel improved es/jp recall@10 by ~0.018 on average (partial), ORT results align with native kernels within 0.005 recall. Next step: run fp16-hybrid for layers [9,10].

Lina Gomez: thanks, please add kmeans centroid shift plots to the PR so we can triage quality vs cost tradeoff. :pray:

Anya Patel: will do. Action items: (1) fp16-hybrid run for layers 9-10 (Anya) (2) add centroid + nn-distance plots to eval artifact (Anya) (3) if still gap, try re-calibration with per-channel clip thresholds (Devendra).

Mike Chen: thx team. keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:
